newsitem.title: UK: BT says no comment on MCI until after review.
newsitem.headline: BT says no comment on MCI until after review.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said Wednesday it would not make any comment on the future of its planned acquisition of MCI Communications Inc. until it completes a full-scale review of the telecommunications carrier's prospects.

Still reeling from an unexpected profit warning by MCI last week that rocked the $24 billion merger plan, a BT spokesman confirmed that a review of the proposed combination would be headed by the two companies' chief executives, Sir Peter Bonfield and Gerry Taylor.
"Until such a time as the review is completed, we cannot comment on the future of this merger," the spokesman said.
Asked how long the investigation would take, the spokesman said, "How long is a piece of string?"
The review was likely to start immediately, with Bonfield set to fly to the United States in the next few days -- after presiding over BT's annual shareholder meeting Wednesday.
"It's a matter of great urgency, and our shareholders want to know what is going on. ... We will make a statement when we have something to say," the spokesman said.
MCI, the second biggest U.S. long-distance carrier, said last week that it expected to ring up substantially larger than expected losses in trying to enter local U.S. phone markets.
Washington-based MCI warned of an additional $500 million losses this year and an extra $700 million to $1 billion in 1998.
Despite its problems in gaining access to the potentially lucrative local markets, MCI said it planned to substantially step up investment.

BT, which has been under pressure from insitutional shareholers to investigate whether the terms of the merger should be renegotiated after a sharp fall in the companies' stock prices, says there may be other and cheaper ways of entering local U.S. markets.

The company denied a report in The Wall Street Journal that changes in MCI's local U.S. business could not be considered a "material adverse" event and thus be grounds to prompt new terms for the deal.
BT has also denied that MCI shareholders received early warnings in March of problems breaking into local markets that were not disclosed to BT.
BT says it first heard of the new forecast losses last Wednesday, and promptly issued a statement to its own shareholders the following day.
